correctness.rationale: The parity decomposition of the quotient deck group yields exactly two squared Euclidean distance expressions; circular-distance pairs admit a coordinatewise dominating edge. One-dimensional optimization across its four segments gives the explicit eccentricity function with a rigorously checked threshold. Branch derivatives are nonpositive and strictly negative away from endpoints, leading to the complete center/diameter classification. The two rational branch derivatives of normalized squared radius have exactly one positive stationary minimum in each region, equal to \(2/(3\sqrt3)\), with two nonisometric equality metrics. Exact-rational independent Voronoi-vertex calculations for 11 instances corroborate but do not establish universality.

value.rationale: The metric radius is a natural global invariant in Riemannian geometry, distinct from systole and injectivity radius. The result gives a complete moduli profile, full minimizing and maximizing center loci, an aspect-dependent farthest-point transition and a sharp scale-invariant area inequality with precisely two nonisometric optimizers. These are structural classification results, not a parameter substitution or a narrow preselected numerical benchmark.
